name: API Design
description: Enforces RESTful API conventions including proper status codes, pagination, and error formats.
content:
# API Design Rules

- Use RESTful resource naming — plural nouns (`/users`, `/orders`), not verbs (`/getUsers`)
- Use correct HTTP methods: GET (read), POST (create), PUT (full update), PATCH (partial update), DELETE (remove)
- Return proper status codes: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 422 Unprocessable Entity, 429 Too Many Requests, 500 Internal Server Error
- Implement cursor-based pagination for list endpoints — include `next_cursor` and `has_more` in responses
- Use consistent error response format: `{ "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "...", "details": [] } }`
- Version APIs in the URL path (`/v1/users`) or via headers — never break existing clients
- Use `snake_case` for JSON field names in Python/Ruby APIs, `camelCase` for JavaScript/TypeScript APIs
- Include `Content-Type` and `Accept` headers — validate them on the server
- Implement idempotency keys for POST/PATCH endpoints to handle retries safely
- Document every endpoint with OpenAPI/Swagger — include request/response examples
